subcompetencies.name: Antepartum Care and Complications of Pregnancy

level_1: Demonstrates basic knowledge of normal obstetrical care and common medical complications seen in pregnancy
Effectively supervises and educates lower- level residents in antepartum care
level_2: Provides complete antepartum care for women with uncomplicated pregnancies
Recognizes atypical presentations of medical and obstetrical complications; identifies indications for referral and/or transfer of care for patients with medical and obstetrical complications
level_3: Recognizes basic risk factors, symptoms, and signs of common medical and obstetrical complications
Manages patients with complex and atypical medical and obstetrical complications and implements treatment plans based on emerging evidence
level_4: Provides complete antepartum care for women with complicated pregnancies
level_5: Manages common medical and obstetrical complications

level_1: Formulates a differential diagnosis for patients with first-trimester bleeding
level_2: Counsels patients regarding natural history, and diagnostic and treatment options
level_3: Uses non-surgical and surgical methods to manage patients with first-trimester bleeding
level_4: Manages patients with complications of first- trimester bleeding
level_5: Implements treatment plans for complex or atypical first-trimester bleeding

subcompetencies.name: Care of Patients in the Intrapartum Period

level_1: Demonstrates basic knowledge of routine/uncomplicated intrapartum obstetrical care, including conduct of normal labor
Manages common labor and intrapartum complications
level_2: Performs basic obstetric skills (e.g., identification of fetal lie, interpretation of fetal heart rate monitoring, and tocodynamometry)
Provides care for women with complex intrapartum complications and conditions
level_3: Manages normal labor
Identifies indications for referral and/or transfer of care for patients with intrapartum complications
level_4: Recognizes common intrapartum complications
Applies innovative approaches to complex and atypical intrapartum conditions and implements treatment plans based on emerging evidence
level_5: Effectively supervises and educates lower-level residents in intrapartum care for women with uncomplicated pregnancies

subcompetencies.name: Care of Patients in the Postpartum and Interconception Period

level_1: Provides postpartum and interconception care for women with uncomplicated pregnancies
level_2: Recognizes basic risk factors, symptoms, and signs of common postpartum and interconception complications
level_3: Manages common postpartum complications and counsels patients about associated risk in future pregnancies
level_4: Manages patients with complex postpartum complications and identifies indications for referral and/or transfer of care in the postpartum or interconception period
level_5: Applies innovative approaches to complex and atypical postpartum and interconception conditions and implements treatment plans based on emerging evidence

level_1: Demonstrates basic surgical principles, including use of universal precautions and aseptic technique
level_2: Demonstrates basic obstetrical skills
level_3: Performs advanced obstetrical procedures
level_4: Performs complex obstetrical procedures
level_5: Applies innovative and complex approaches obstetrical care and implements treatment plans based on emerging evidence

subcompetencies.name: Critically Ill Obstetric Patients and Obstetric Emergencies

level_1: Recognizes risk factors that can lead to critical illness in an obstetric patient
Manages and treats obstetric emergencies
level_2: Recognizes risk factors for obstetric emergencies
Collaborates with other health care teams to facilitate care for critically ill obstetric patients
level_3: Formulates an initial differential diagnosis, recognizes initial signs/symptoms of a critically ill patient (vital signs, lab abnormalities, etc.) and asks for assistance in a timely fashion
Leads the multidisciplinary health care team in caring for patients with obstetric emergencies
level_4: Recognizes obstetric emergencies and asks for assistance in a timely fashion
Debriefs with the members of the health care team, the patient, and the family members of a critically ill obstetric patient
level_5: Manages and initiates treatment for a critically ill obstetric patient, including recognizing when a transfer to the intensive care unit (ICU) or another service is most appropriate
Debriefs with the members of the health care team, the patient, and the patient’s family members after an obstetric emergency

level_1: Identifies alterations in normal physiology and anatomy
level_2: Accurately and reliably gathers and reports clinical information pertaining to common peri-procedural risks and complications
level_3: Independently identifies and manages common peri-procedural risks and complications
level_4: Independently identifies and manages complex peri-procedural risks and complications
level_5: Implements measures to prevent or mitigate complications, applying effective interdisciplinary team management skills to manage multiple scenarios simultaneously

level_1: Prepares patient and equipment for endoscopic procedures (e.g., lithotomy positioning, assemble endoscope)
level_2: Performs diagnostic hysteroscopy and cystoscopy
level_3: Independently performs simple operative hysteroscopic procedures
level_4: Independently performs complex operative hysteroscopic procedures
level_5: Independently performs complex hysteroscopic procedures in altered anatomy

level_1: Demonstrates basic skills (e.g., positioning, draping, docking, undocking)
level_2: Assists during laparoscopic procedures (e.g., port placement, bedside assistant)
level_3: Independently performs simple laparoscopic procedures
level_4: Independently performs advanced laparoscopic procedures
level_5: Independently performs uncommon complex laparoscopic procedures

level_1: Demonstrates basic skills (e.g., positioning, knot tying, suturing)
level_2: Performs simple vulvar- vaginal procedures
level_3: Performs pelvic entry for vaginal procedures and simple procedures for incontinence and prolapse
level_4: Independently performs vaginal hysterectomy and complex vulvar- vaginal procedures
level_5: Independently performs uncommon complex vulvar-vaginal procedures

level_1: Demonstrates basic skills (e.g., positioning, knot tying, suturing)
level_2: Opens and closes abdominal incisions
level_3: Independently performs simple open surgical procedures
level_4: Independently performs complex open surgical procedures
level_5: Independently performs uncommon complex open surgical procedures

level_1: Demonstrates ability to find reputable, evidence- based information on contraception choices
Implements comprehensive management plans for patients with medical conditions complicating their use of contraceptive methods
level_2: Counsels patients on the effectiveness, risks, benefits, and contraindications of available forms of family planning
Performs surgical uterine evacuation on patients with complex comorbidities and manages complications
level_3: Performs medical uterine evacuation
Applies innovative and complex approaches to medical contraception and pregnancy termination, and implements treatment plans based on emerging evidence
level_4: Implements comprehensive contraception management plans for patients and manages common side effects
level_5: Performs routine surgical uterine evacuation and manages complications

level_1: Takes a focused patient history for common ambulatory gynecologic problems
level_2: Performs the initial assessment, formulates a differential diagnosis, and initiates treatment, including performance of basic procedures for common ambulatory gynecologic problems
level_3: Formulates management plans and initiates treatment, including relevant procedures for complex ambulatory gynecologic problems
level_4: Effectively cares for patients with complex presentations and uses a multidisciplinary approach when caring for patients with complex problems
level_5: Applies innovative approaches to complex and atypical ambulatory gynecology and implements treatment plans based on emerging evidence

level_1: Performs consultation, with guidance
level_2: Triages consult requests 	Manages consultations (including coordination of care) requiring intervention, including procedural options
level_3: Supervises lower-level residents in managing consultations (including coordination of care) requiring intervention, including procedural options
level_4: Oversees the consultation process and manages interdisciplinary systems issues affecting patient care

subcompetencies.name: Anatomy and Pathophysiology of Female Reproduction

level_1: Identifies normal anatomy relevant to physical examination, imaging, and surgery
Demonstrates advanced knowledge of pathophysiology and clinical findings for common diseases of the reproductive system
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of physiology of reproduction
Identifies complex pathologic anatomic variants during surgery
level_3: Identifies pathologic anatomic variants as applied to physical examination and imaging
Demonstrates comprehensive knowledge of the varying patterns of disease presentation, natural history, and patient outcomes
level_4: Demonstrates basic knowledge of pathophysiology and clinical findings for common diseases of the reproductive system
Contributes to peer- reviewed literature on the varying patterns of disease presentation, and natural history
level_5: Identifies common pathologic anatomic variants during surgery

level_1: Generates a basic differential diagnosis based on patient symptoms and history
level_2: Generates a comprehensive differential diagnosis based on patient symptoms and history and interpretation of results of common diagnostic tests
level_3: Generates a prioritized differential diagnosis and selects additional testing for confirmation
level_4: Independently and efficiently synthesizes information to develop prioritized differential diagnoses in complex patient presentations and incorporates subtle, unusual, or conflicting findings
level_5: Coaches peers to develop prioritized differential diagnoses in atypical patient presentations

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common patient safety events
Participates in disclosure of patient safety events to patients and their families (simulated or actual)
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of how to report patient safety events
Conducts analysis of patient safety events and offers error prevention strategies (simulated or actual)
level_3: Identifies system factors that lead to patient safety events
Discloses patient safety events to patients and their families (simulated or actual)
level_4: Reports patient safety events through institutional reporting systems (simulated or actual)
Actively engages teams and processes to modify systems to prevent patient safety events
level_5: Participates in analysis of patient safety events (simulated or actual)
Role models or mentors others in the disclosure of patient safety events

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of basic quality improvement methodologies and metrics
level_2: Describes local quality improvement initiatives (e.g., cancer screening rate, surgical site infection, smoking cessation)
level_3: Participates in local quality improvement initiatives
level_4: Demonstrates the skills required to identify, develop, implement, and analyze a quality improvement project
level_5: Creates, implements, and assesses quality improvement initiatives at the institutional or community level

subcompetencies.name: System Navigation for Patient-Centered Care - Coordination of Care

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of care coordination
level_2: Coordinates care of patients in routine clinical situations effectively using the roles of interprofessional team members
level_3: Coordinates care of patients in complex clinical situations effectively using the roles of interprofessional team members
level_4: Identifies concerns with current systems and identifies opportunities for improvement
level_5: Analyzes the process of care coordination and leads in the design and implementation of improvements

subcompetencies.name: System Navigation for Patient-Centered Care – Transitions of Care

level_1: Identifies key elements for safe and effective transitions of care and hand-offs
level_2: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in routine clinical situations
level_3: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in complex clinical situations
level_4: Role models and advocates for safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs within and across health care delivery systems, including in outpatient settings
level_5: Improves quality of transitions of care within and across health care delivery systems to optimize patient outcomes

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of population and community health needs
level_2: Identifies specific population and community health needs for their local population
level_3: Uses local resources effectively to meet the needs of a patient population and community
level_4: Participates in changing and adapting practice to provide for the needs of specific populations
level_5: Leads innovations and advocates for populations and communities with specific health care needs

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Identifies key components of the complex health care system (e.g., hospital, skilled nursing facility, finance, personnel, technology)
level_2: Describes how components of a complex health care system are interrelated and how this impacts patient care
level_3: Discusses how individual practice affects the broader system (e.g., length of stay, readmission rates, clinical efficiency)
level_4: Manages various components of the complex health care system to provide efficient and effective patient care and transitions of care
level_5: Advocates for or leads systems change that enhances high-value, efficient, and effective patient care and transitions of care

level_1: Demonstrates how to access and use available evidence and incorporate patient preferences and values to the care of a routine patient
level_2: Articulates clinical questions and elicits patient preferences and values to guide evidence- based care, with guidance from other health care team members
level_3: Locates and applies the best available evidence, integrated with patient preferences, to the care of complex patients, with minimal guidance
level_4: Critically appraises and applies evidence, even in the face of uncertainty and conflicting evidence, to guide care tailored to the individual patient
level_5: Coaches others to critically appraise and apply evidence for complex patients and/or participates in the development of guidelines

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Identifies gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Integrates practice data and feedback with humility to implement a learning plan
level_2: Establishes goals for personal and professional development
Continuously reflects on remaining gaps and institutes behavioral adjustments to narrow them
level_3: Analyzes and reflects on the factors that contribute to gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Uses performance data to measure the effectiveness of the learning plan and adapts when necessary
level_4: Identifies opportunities for performance improvement; designs a learning plan
Coaches others on reflective practice
level_5: Institutes behavioral change(s) to narrow the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Coaches others in the design and implementation of learning plans

level_1: Identifies and describes potential triggers for professionalism lapses and how to appropriately report professionalism lapses
level_2: Demonstrates insight into professional behavior in routine situations and takes responsibility for one’s own professionalism lapses
level_3: Demonstrates professional behavior in complex or stressful situations
level_4: Recognizes situations that may trigger professionalism lapses and intervenes to prevent lapses in oneself and others
level_5: Coaches others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of ethical principles
level_2: Analyzes straightforward situations using ethical principles
level_3: Recognizes the need to seek help in managing and resolving complex ethical situations
level_4: Recognizes and uses appropriate resources for managing and resolving ethical dilemmas as needed and identifies system- level issues that induce or exacerbate ethical problems
level_5: Seeks to address system- level factors that induce or exacerbate ethical problems or impede their resolution

level_1: Takes responsibility for failure to complete tasks and responsibilities, identifies potential contributing factors, and describes strategies for ensuring timely task completion in the future
Proactively implements strategies to ensure that the needs of patients, teams, and systems are met
level_2: Responds promptly to requests or reminders to complete tasks and responsibilities
Recognizes situations that may impact others’ ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
level_3: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in routine situations

Recognizes one’s own role in leading the care of all patients on the service while mentoring/coaching other team members to ensure the best possible care of patients, including prioritizing tasks and mitigating burnout
level_4: Recognizes situations that may impact one’s own ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
level_5: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in complex or stressful situations

level_1: Recognizes status of personal and professional well-being, with assistance
level_2: Independently recognizes status of personal and professional well-being
level_3: With assistance, proposes a plan to optimize personal and professional well-being
level_4: Independently develops a plan to optimize personal and professional well-being
level_5: Coaches others when emotional responses or limitations in knowledge/skills do not meet professional expectations

level_1: Demonstrates respect and establishes rapport with patients and patients’ families (e.g., situational awareness of language, disability, health literacy level, cultural differences)
When prompted, reflects on biases while attempting to minimize communication barriers
level_2: Communicates with patients and their families in an understandable and respectful manner
Facilitates difficult discussions specific to conferences with patients and patients’ families (e.g., end-of- life, explaining complications, therapeutic uncertainty)
level_3: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in straightforward encounters
Independently recognizes biases while attempting to proactively minimize communication barriers
level_4: Identifies barriers to effective communication (e.g., health literacy, cultural differences)
Mentors others in situational awareness and critical self-reflection
level_5: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in challenging encounters (e.g., shared decision-making)
Coaches others in the facilitation of crucial conversations

level_1: Demonstrates basic understanding of the informed consent process
level_2: Answers questions about the treatment plan and seeks guidance when appropriate
level_3: Counsels patients through the decision-making process, including responding to questions, for simple clinical problems
level_4: Counsels patients through the decision- making process, including responding to questions, for complex clinical problems
level_5: Counsels patients through the decision-making process, including responding to questions, for uncommon clinical problems

level_1: Understands and respects the role and function of interprofessional team members
Integrates contributions from other health care team members into the care plan
level_2: Understands and respects the role and function of other health care team members
Prevents and mediates conflict and distress among interprofessional team members
level_3: Solicits insights from and uses language that values all interprofessional team members
Addresses conflict and distress among other health care team members in complex patient situations
level_4: Solicits insights from other health care team members using language that values all members
Fosters a culture of open communication and effective teamwork within the interprofessional team
level_5: Integrates contributions from interprofessional team members into the care plan
Attends to individual and team distress and promotes resilience among other health care teams

level_1: Accurately records information in the patient record
Appropriately selects direct (e.g., telephone, in- person) and indirect (e.g., progress notes, text messages) forms of communication based on context
level_2: Safeguards patient personal health information
Communicates clearly, concisely, on time, and in an organized written form, including providing anticipatory guidance
level_3: Demonstrates organized diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning through notes in the patient record
Produces written or verbal communication (e.g., patient notes, emails) that serves as an example for others to follow
level_4: Documents required data in formats specified by institutional policy
Models feedback to improve others’ written communication
level_5: Concisely reports diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning in the patient record in an efficient manner
Guides departmental or institutional communication around policies and procedures
